detail.body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Under CUDA graphs the fused compact DSA indexer (`--dsa-kernel-backend cudnn`, `--dsa-indexer-precision mxfp8`) keeps a persistent workspace per static geometry (MXFP8 q/k quantization destinations, packed scales, candidate offsets) that must be prepared outside capture. Every CSA layer owned its own copy: about 7 GiB per rank on DSv4 at 16K tokens per rank.

- All CSA layers built from one `TransformerConfig` now share one workspace per geometry and balanced-indexer slot (`_CompactIndexerWorkspaceStore`, keyed on the config). The layers of a graph run serially on one stream and nothing in the workspace outlives the indexer dispatch that fills it, so sharing only removes duplicates.
- New config field `dsa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing` (default `True`; `--no-dsa-compact-indexer-workspace-sharing` restores per-layer workspaces), golden-config entry, doc paragraph in `cuda_graph.md`.
- Tests: kernel-level workspace tests (`test_csa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing.py`) and a contract test in the CSA test class that a workspace prepared by one layer serves the capture of another.

Validation: GB200, 4 ranks: CSA test files 118 passed. DSv4-flash 1M on 128 GPUs with chunk-wise graphs: last-stage NVML memory 173.8 → 149.4 GiB together with linear CE (#5258 validation).

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: <!-- e.g. Fixes #1234 / Related to #1234 -->

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

@@ -2009,6 +2009,49 @@ class CompressedSparseAttentionSubmodules:
     indexer: Union[ModuleSpec, type] = None
 
 
+class _CompactIndexerWorkspaceStore:
+    """Warmed-up compact-indexer workspaces (BSHD, THD, balanced THD per slot) and the active one
+    of each kind (the immediately preceding warm-up, which capture reuses).
+
+    One store per CSA module reproduces the historical per-layer ownership. With
+    ``TransformerConfig.dsa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing`` all CSA modules built from the same
+    config on the same device share one store: layers execute serially on one stream and nothing in
+    a workspace outlives the indexer dispatch that fills it (the quantized q/k, packed scales and
+    candidate offsets are consumed by the compact top-k kernel, whose outputs are copied into
+    per-dispatch buffers; the attention and indexer-loss backward read bf16 saved tensors, never
+    the workspace), so a later layer overwriting the buffers is the same reuse eager gets from
+    its transient allocations.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.bshd: list[BSHDCompactIndexerWorkspace] = []
+        self.bshd_active: BSHDCompactIndexerWorkspace | None = None
+        self.thd: list[THDCompactIndexerWorkspace] = []
+        self.thd_active: THDCompactIndexerWorkspace | None = None
+        self.balanced_thd: dict[str, list[THDCompactIndexerWorkspace]] = {}
+        self.balanced_thd_active: dict[str, THDCompactIndexerWorkspace] = {}
+
+    def __deepcopy__(self, memo):
+        # Runtime GPU state shared by graphs; a copied config must not duplicate it.
+        return self
+
+
+def _shared_compact_indexer_workspace_store(config, device: torch.device):
+    """Return the store shared by all CSA layers built from ``config`` on ``device``."""
+    stores = getattr(config, "_compact_indexer_workspace_stores", None)
+    if stores is None:
+        stores = {}
+        # Plain attribute on the (non-frozen) dataclass: not a field, so it is invisible to
+        # ``dataclasses.asdict``/``replace``; ``__deepcopy__`` above keeps copies from cloning it.
+        setattr(config, "_compact_indexer_workspace_stores", stores)
+    key = (device.type, device.index)
+    store = stores.get(key)
+    if store is None:
+        store = _CompactIndexerWorkspaceStore()
+        stores[key] = store
+    return store
+

+# Copyright (c) 2025, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved.
+"""Cross-layer sharing of the compact DSA indexer workspace under CUDA graphs: real kernels.
+(The sharing contract itself is tested next to the other compact-workspace tests in
+``test_attention_variant_csa.py::TestCompressedSparseAttentionThd``.)"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+
+class TestCompactIndexerWorkspaceSharingKernels:
+    """Real compact-indexer kernels: two layers dispatched through one shared workspace must produce
+    exactly what each produces through its own workspace (stale content from the other layer must
+    not leak: quantize overwrites the staging buffers, the top-k kernel reads only them)."""
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("precision", ["bf16", "mxfp8"])
+    def test_interleaved_layers_through_one_workspace_match_private_workspaces(self, precision):
+        import inspect
+
+        from megatron.core.transformer.experimental_attention_variant.csa_utils import (
+            fused_sparse_attention as dk,
+        )
+        from tests.unit_tests.transformer.experimental_attention_variant import (
+            test_csa_fused_sparse_attention as fsa_tests,
+        )
+
+        fsa_tests._skip_if_real_kernels_unavailable()
+        if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10:
+            pytest.skip("compact THD indexer forward + Top-K requires SM100+")
+        from cudnn import DSA
+
+        if not hasattr(DSA, 'compress_topk_cand_buffer_size_thd'):
+            pytest.skip("installed cuDNN Frontend lacks the compact THD workspace helper")
+        compact_wrapper = getattr(DSA, "indexer_forward_top_k_wrapper", None)
+        mxfp8_parameters = {"q_scale", "cu_seqlens_q_scale_padded", "cu_seqlens_k_scale_padded"}
+        if precision == "mxfp8" and mxfp8_parameters - set(
+            inspect.signature(compact_wrapper).parameters if callable(compact_wrapper) else ()
+        ):
+            pytest.skip("installed cuDNN Frontend lacks compact MXFP8 indexer support")
+
+        ratio, topk, idx_nh, idx_hd = 4, 16, 64, 128
+        q_lens, k_lens = [64, 96], [16, 24]
+        max_seqlen_q, max_seqlen_k = 96, 24
+        cu_q = fsa_tests._make_cu_seqlens(q_lens, device='cuda')
+        cu_k = fsa_tests._make_cu_seqlens(k_lens, device='cuda')
+        total_q, total_k = sum(q_lens), sum(k_lens)
+        sm_scale = idx_hd**-0.5
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        layers = []
+        for _ in range(2):  # two "layers" with the same geometry and different values
+            q = torch.randn(total_q, idx_nh, idx_hd, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
+            k = torch.randn(total_k, idx_hd, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda')
+            w = torch.randn(total_q, idx_nh, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device='cuda').float() * sm_scale
+            layers.append((q, k, w.to(torch.bfloat16)))
+
+        def prepare(q, k):
+            return dk.prepare_thd_compact_indexer_workspace(
+                q,
+                k,
+                topk=topk,
+                ratio=ratio,
+                cu_seqlens_q=cu_q,
+                cu_seqlens_k=cu_k,
+                max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen_q,
+                max_seqlen_k=max_seqlen_k,
+                return_softmax=True,
+                precision=precision,
+            )
+
+        def run(q, k, w, workspace):
+            indices, lengths, _, softmax = dk._indexer_topk_core(
+                q,
+                k,
+                w,
+                topk=topk,
+                ratio=ratio,
+                cu_seqlens_q=cu_q,
+                cu_seqlens_kv=cu_k,
+                max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen_q,
+                max_seqlen_kv=max_seqlen_k,
+                use_compact=True,
+                return_softmax=True,
+                compact_workspace=workspace,
+                precision=precision,
+            )
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            return indices.clone(), lengths.clone(), softmax.clone()
+
+        private = [prepare(q, k) for q, k, _ in layers]
+        shared = prepare(*layers[0][:2])  # the geometry is the same for both layers
+        assert shared is not None and all(ws is not None for ws in private)
+        # cuDNN Frontend: eager calls perform value validation and JIT compilation first.
+        for _ in range(3):
+            run(*layers[0], private[0])
+        reference = [run(*layers[i], private[i]) for i in (0, 1)]
+        # Interleave the two layers through the one shared workspace: every dispatch finds the
+        # other layer's stale quantized q/k and scales in the buffers.
+        for i in (0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0):
+            indices, lengths, softmax = run(*layers[i], shared)
+            assert torch.equal(indices, reference[i][0])
+            assert torch.equal(lengths, reference[i][1])
+            assert torch.equal(softmax, reference[i][2])

**[SUGGESTION Consistency]** The BSHD capture path still accepts only the *active* workspace, while THD now scans every warmed-up workspace.

**Failure.** The new THD comment ([L2359-L2362](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L2359-L2362)) says that under full activation recompute, the no-grad forward and its recompute alternate between two geometries. The BSHD path alternates the same way:
- **No-grad forward:** `forward` goes to `_forward_fused_indexer_inference`, which asks for a workspace with `return_softmax=False` ([L2607](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L2607)).
- **Recompute with grad:** it goes to `_forward_fused_indexer_training`, which uses `return_softmax=indexer_loss_coeff > 0 and sparse_loss` ([L2674-L2680](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L2674-L2680)).

`BSHDCompactIndexerWorkspace.matches_shape` compares `return_softmax`. However, the capture branch ([L2284-L2292](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L2284-L2292)) only tries `self._active_bshd_compact_indexer_workspace`.

Trigger: warm up with `return_softmax=False`, then warm up with `True`, then capture the `False` geometry. The capture raises `ValueError: BSHD compact CUDA graph capture requires an eagerly prepared compact workspace...`, even though a matching workspace is already in `_bshd_compact_indexer_workspaces`. With sharing on (the default), the active slot now holds the last warm-up done by *any* CSA layer on the device. The base code already checked only the active workspace, so this is not a regression from sharing. It is the same failure the PR fixes for THD, left in place for BSHD.

**Correction.** Replace the capturing branch of `_get_bshd_compact_indexer_workspace` with the same candidate scan the THD path uses:
```python
        capturing = torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
        workspace = self._active_bshd_compact_indexer_workspace
        if capturing:
            # As in the THD path: the last warm-up may have prepared the other recompute
            # geometry. Matching is shape-only (no host synchronization).
            candidates = [workspace] if workspace is not None else []
            candidates += [w for w in self._bshd_compact_indexer_workspaces if w is not workspace]
            for candidate in candidates:
                if candidate.matches_shape(**match_kwargs):
                    self._active_bshd_compact_indexer_workspace = candidate
                    return candidate
            raise ValueError(
                "BSHD compact CUDA graph capture requires an eagerly prepared compact "
                "workspace for the active static geometry. Run eager warmup before capture."
            )
```
Invariant: during capture, return any eagerly prepared workspace whose static geometry matches. Never prepare one during capture, because preparing needs a host sync.

**Preservation.** The existing test `test_bshd_compact_workspace_prepared_in_warmup_and_reused_in_capture` (test_attention_variant_csa.py L900-L953) should still pass. Warm-up sees an empty list and prepares once; capture has exactly one candidate. So `workspace.matches_shape.assert_called_once()` and `_bshd_compact_indexer_workspaces == [workspace]` still hold. A capture with no matching warm-up still raises `ValueError`.

**Acceptance (proposed test, not run).**
- Setup: set `dsa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing=False` and patch `bshd_compact_indexer_available` to return `True`.
- Patch `prepare_bshd_compact_indexer_workspace` with `side_effect=[ws_f, ws_t]`. These are MagicMocks whose `matches_shape` returns `kwargs["return_softmax"] is False` and `is True` respectively.
- Patch `is_current_stream_capturing` with `side_effect=[False, False, True]`.
- Steps: call with `return_softmax=False`, then `True`, then capture with `False`.
- Expected: the third call returns `ws_f` and `prepare` was called twice. Today the third call raises `ValueError`.

- **Docstring ([L2331-L2334](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L2331-L2334)):** it says "Capture reuses the active workspace". Capture now tries the active workspace first and then every warmed-up workspace in the slot ([L2363-L2385](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa.py#L2363-L2385)).

With `dsa_compact_indexer_workspace_sharing=True` (the new default), modules no longer own their storage independently. Only the separation between head and tail slots remains.

A wrong comment here will mislead the next person debugging a capture failure. Suggested replacement for both:

```python
        other warmed-up workspace of the same slot whose static geometry matches;
        when none matches (warmup skipped or static shapes changed), capture must
        fail clearly. Unsupported devices/frontends retain the non-compact path.
        """
        ...
        # Head and tail have different causal offsets and may have different
        # geometry. Keep their quantization/candidate metadata in separate slots;
        # each slot is shared by every CSA layer bound to the same workspace store.
```

<!-- nemo-ci-review-impact:v1 ceiling=low -->

## Strict review: share the fused compact DSA indexer workspace across CSA layers

**Findings:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 2 (both posted inline)

**Risk: low.** Sharing one workspace across layers looks safe. I traced the workspace from the point it is written to every point it is read:

- **Quantization buffers:** the MXFP8 quantization destinations and packed scales are overwritten on every dispatch.
- **Per-dispatch refresh:** `cand_batch_offsets` and the MXFP8 scale offsets (`cu_seqlens_*_scale_padded`) are rewritten in place on every dispatch ([fused_sparse_attention.py L1875-L1877, L1925-L1930](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L1875-L1930)).
- **Scratch and outputs:** candidate scratch and the compact outputs are allocated per dispatch, and a check confirms the kernel wrote into those per-dispatch buffers ([L540-L566](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L540-L566), [L1974-L1990](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/experimental_attention_variant/csa_utils/fused_sparse_attention.py#L1974-L1990)).
- **Backward:** the sparse-attention backward saves `q`, `kv`, `topk_idxs`, `out` and `lse`, never the workspace.
- **Ordering:** with the local CUDA graph implementation, each graph's warm-up runs right before its own capture ([cuda_graphs.py L930-L980](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/core/transformer/cuda_graphs.py#L930-L980)). Changing who owns the "active" workspace therefore does not change which workspace a capture sees.

So a later layer overwriting the shared buffers is the same reuse that eager mode already does.

The new config field is read in `_compact_indexer_workspace_store`, so it is not dead code. Its `--no-`/`--disable-` CLI flags are generated automatically by `ArgumentGroupFactory` ([argument_utils.py L199-L211](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/training/argument_utils.py#L199-L211), [arguments.py L2861](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/813286f86ad9a0f2d47013bdb6889a905915907a/megatron/training/arguments.py#L2861)). The golden-config entry is updated.

**Suggestions (inline):**
1. **BSHD capture path:** it still accepts only the active workspace, while the THD path now scans every warmed-up workspace. The full-recompute geometry alternation described in the new THD comment applies to BSHD unchanged. This already existed before the PR and is not caused by sharing. Mirroring the THD scan is a short change, and the patch is in the inline comment.
2. **Stale comments in `_get_thd_compact_indexer_workspace`:** two unchanged comments now contradict the code. The docstring says capture reuses only the active workspace. Another comment says each attention module owns its storage independently, which is no longer true with the default sharing.

**Limitations:**
- The skill's `style-guide.md` is not in the base tree (`/context/base/style-guide.md` and `/context/base/skills/style-guide.md` are both missing), so no style-guide audit was done.
- I could not search the whole repo for code that assigns to the now read-only `_*_compact_indexer_workspaces` attributes. I spot-checked `cuda_graphs.py`, `cp_balanced_indexer.py` and the DSv4 CP CUDA graph tests and found no such assignments.
- None of the suggested code has been run.
